<skills_instructions>
## Skills
A skill is a set of local instructions to follow that is stored in a `SKILL.md` file. Below is the list of skills that can be used. Each entry includes a name, description, and a short path that can be expanded into an absolute path using the skill roots table.
### Skill roots
- `r0` = `/control/codex/skills/.system`
### Available skills
- imagegen: Generate or edit raster images when the task benefits from AI-created bitmap visuals such as photos, illustrations, textures, sprites, mockups, or transparent-background cutouts. Use when Codex should create a brand-new image, transform an existing image, or derive visual variants from references, and the output should be a bitmap asset rather than repo-native code or vector. Do not use when the task is better handled by editing existing SVG/vector/code-native assets, extending an established icon or logo system, or building the visual directly in HTML/CSS/canvas. (file: r0/imagegen/SKILL.md)
- openai-docs: Use for Codex models/pricing, scheduled tasks, skills, settings, setup, troubleshooting, customization, automations, and self-knowledge—including 'you,' 'your,' 'this app,' or 'this coding agent' when they refer to Codex—and for OpenAI APIs/products and ChatGPT Work. Also use for model choice/migration, prompting, SDKs, Responses, Realtime, agents, evals, and Chat/Work/Codex comparisons. Do not use for generic app/software tasks that merely mention Codex. (file: r0/openai-docs/SKILL.md)
- plugin-creator: Create and scaffold plugin directories for Codex with a required `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, optional plugin folders/files, valid manifest defaults, and personal-marketplace entries by default. Use when Codex needs to create a new personal plugin, add optional plugin structure, generate or update marketplace entries for plugin ordering and availability metadata, or update an existing local plugin during development with the CLI-driven cachebuster and reinstall flow. (file: r0/plugin-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-creator: Create or update a Codex skill with appropriately scoped instructions and any needed supporting resources. (file: r0/skill-creator/SKILL.md)
- skill-installer: Install Codex skills into $CODEX_HOME/skills from a curated list or a GitHub repo path. Use when a user asks to list installable skills, install a curated skill, or install a skill from another repo (including private repos). (file: r0/skill-installer/SKILL.md)
</skills_instructions>

{
  "ambiguities": [
    "Nearest rounding allows any minimizer, including either choice at a tie. No deterministic tie-breaking rule is specified.",
    "The model represents numbers as real values, so it does not distinguish signed zeros or include NaNs or infinities. The enlarged rounding set contains arbitrarily large real normalized values, not infinity.",
    "No unresolved ambiguity affects the mathematical translation. The target proof is excluded, so this translation does not audit its proof."
  ],
  "dependency_coverage": [
    {
      "effect_on_target": "This is the summation hypothesis: exact initialization followed by n−1 nearest-rounded additions, with every stored partial sum in the finite representable set.",
      "id": "D001",
      "meaning": "For a format fmt, n∈ℕ, a proof hn that n>0, and p,s:{0,…,n−1}→ℝ, the predicate means s₀=p₀; for every integer index 0≤i<n−1, sᵢ₊₁ is nearest to the exact real sum sᵢ+pᵢ₊₁ in the enlarged set E_fmt of D009; and for every 0≤i<n, sᵢ belongs to F_fmt of D005.",
      "name": "Nearest-rounded sequential summation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Justifies using n−1 as the final index of s; it imposes no additional hypothesis.",
      "id": "D002",
      "meaning": "For every n∈ℕ with n>0, assuming that n−1<n is false yields a contradiction. Subtraction here is natural-number subtraction.",
      "name": "Validity of the final index",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The target universally quantifies over these formats and further restricts the radix to 2.",
      "id": "D003",
      "meaning": "The type of formats, with natural-number radix β and precision t, integer exponent bounds emin and emax, and proofs β≥2, t>0, and emin≤emax, as specified by D011.",
      "name": "Floating-point format",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "The hypothesis sets this parameter equal to 2; it also determines representable values and roundoff.",
      "id": "D004",
      "meaning": "For each format, returns its first field, the radix β∈ℕ.",
      "name": "Radix",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Every input pᵢ and every stored partial sum sᵢ must belong to this set.",
      "id": "D005",
      "meaning": "For fmt and y∈ℝ, F_fmt(y) means y=0, or y is a normalized value as in D013, or y is a subnormal value as in D014.",
      "name": "Finite representable values",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "This is the factor u in the error bound (n−1)u∑ᵢ|pᵢ|; for β=2 it equals 2^(−t).",
      "id": "D006",
      "meaning": "For each format, the real unit roundoff is u=(1/2)ε, where ε=β^(1−t).",
      "name": "Unit roundoff",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes sᵢ a valid array access at every addition step.",
      "id": "D007",
      "meaning": "For every n∈ℕ with n>0 and every i∈Fin(n−1), the underlying natural number i.val is less than n.",
      "name": "Current-step index bound",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes pᵢ₊₁ and sᵢ₊₁ valid array accesses at every addition step.",
      "id": "D008",
      "meaning": "For every n∈ℕ with n>0 and every i∈Fin(n−1), i.val+1<n.",
      "name": "Next-step index bound",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Nearest rounding is measured against this enlarged set, even though the selected stored result must also lie in F_fmt. Rounding is therefore not defined by clamping to the finite range.",
      "id": "D009",
      "meaning": "For fmt and x∈ℝ, E_fmt(x) means F_fmt(x), or there exist a Boolean sign b, m∈ℕ, and e∈ℤ with β^(t−1)≤m<β^t, emax<e, and x=σ(b)mβ^(e−t). Thus it extends the finite set by normalized values at all exponents above emax.",
      "name": "Representable set with unbounded upper exponents",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Determines u through u=ε/2.",
      "id": "D010",
      "meaning": "For each format, ε=β_R^(1−t), where β_R is β embedded in ℝ and 1−t is computed in ℤ.",
      "name": "Machine epsilon",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the built-in domain restrictions on every quantified format; these restrictions need not appear as separate target hypotheses.",
      "id": "D011",
      "meaning": "Given β,t∈ℕ and emin,emax∈ℤ, together with proofs 2≤β, 0<t, and emin≤emax, constructs a format with those fields.",
      "name": "Format constructor and constraints",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies absolute-distance nearest rounding at every step, without choosing a unique minimizer or tie rule.",
      "id": "D012",
      "meaning": "For any predicate S on ℝ and any x,y∈ℝ, y is nearest to x in S exactly when y∈S and, for every z∈ℝ with z∈S, |x−y|≤|x−z|.",
      "name": "Nearest-point relation",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Defines the normalized part of the permitted inputs, partial sums, and rounding set.",
      "id": "D013",
      "meaning": "For fmt and y∈ℝ, y is normalized exactly when there exist b∈Bool, m∈ℕ, and e∈ℤ such that β^(t−1)≤m<β^t, emin≤e≤emax, and y=σ(b)mβ^(e−t).",
      "name": "Normalized representable values",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Includes subnormal values among the permitted inputs, stored sums, and rounding candidates.",
      "id": "D014",
      "meaning": "For fmt and y∈ℝ, y is subnormal exactly when there exist b∈Bool and m∈ℕ with 0<m<β^(t−1) and y=σ(b)mβ^(emin−t).",
      "name": "Subnormal representable values",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supports interpretation of the real numeral 2 in the definition u=(1/2)ε; it is not an extra format assumption.",
      "id": "D015",
      "meaning": "The natural number 1+1 satisfies the predicate of being at least two.",
      "name": "Two is at least two",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Makes radix powers in representable values and roundoff real-valued.",
      "id": "D016",
      "meaning": "For each format, β_R is the natural radix β embedded in ℝ.",
      "name": "Real radix",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Controls the upper limit of the finite set and the threshold beyond which D009 adds further normalized values.",
      "id": "D017",
      "meaning": "For each format, returns its fourth field, emax∈ℤ.",
      "name": "Maximum exponent",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Restricts normalized finite representations to an inclusive interval of exponents.",
      "id": "D018",
      "meaning": "For a format and e∈ℤ, the exponent is in range exactly when emin≤e and e≤emax.",
      "name": "Exponent range",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Restricts normalized significands both in the finite set and in its upper-exponent extension.",
      "id": "D019",
      "meaning": "For a format and m∈ℕ, m is a normalized mantissa exactly when β^(t−1)≤m and m<β^t.",
      "name": "Normalized mantissa range",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the precise exponent convention for normalized values: the scale is β^(e−t).",
      "id": "D020",
      "meaning": "For any format, Boolean b, m∈ℕ, and e∈ℤ, the normalized-value expression is (σ(b)·(m cast to ℝ))·β_R^(e−(t cast to ℤ)). This function itself imposes no mantissa or exponent range restriction.",
      "name": "Normalized value formula",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Specifies the nonzero subnormal significands; the range is empty when t=1.",
      "id": "D021",
      "meaning": "For a format and m∈ℕ, m is a subnormal mantissa exactly when 0<m<β^(t−1).",
      "name": "Subnormal mantissa range",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Fixes the subnormal spacing at β^(emin−t).",
      "id": "D022",
      "meaning": "For any format, Boolean b, and m∈ℕ, the subnormal-value expression is (σ(b)·(m cast to ℝ))·β_R^(emin−(t cast to ℤ)). This function itself imposes no mantissa restriction.",
      "name": "Subnormal value formula",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Controls mantissa ranges and the constant u; it is any positive natural number.",
      "id": "D023",
      "meaning": "For each format, returns its second field, the precision t∈ℕ.",
      "name": "Precision",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Controls the lower normalized exponent and the fixed subnormal scale.",
      "id": "D024",
      "meaning": "For each format, returns its third field, emin∈ℤ.",
      "name": "Minimum exponent",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Supplies the strict upper bound on normalized mantissas.",
      "id": "D025",
      "meaning": "For a format and m∈ℕ, the mantissa-range predicate is m<β^t, with natural-number exponentiation.",
      "name": "Mantissa upper bound",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Separates subnormal mantissas from normalized mantissas.",
      "id": "D026",
      "meaning": "For each format, the minimum normalized mantissa is the natural number β^(t−1). Here t−1 is natural-number subtraction, agreeing with ordinary subtraction because t>0.",
      "name": "Minimum normalized mantissa",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Allows positive and negative representable values; its format argument has no effect.",
      "id": "D027",
      "meaning": "For any format and Boolean b, σ(b)=−1 if b=true and σ(b)=1 otherwise.",
      "name": "Sign multiplier",
      "status": "understood"
    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Converts D002 into a proof that n−1<n for construction of the final index.",

      "meaning": "For any proposition P with a decision procedure, if ¬P implies falsehood, then P holds.",

    },
    {
      "effect_on_target": "Expresses β=2, s₀=p₀, representation equalities, and the Boolean sign test.",
      "id": "D029",
      "meaning": "For any type or sort α and x,y∈α, Eq(x,y) is the proposition that x and y are equal.",

      "effect_on_target": "Makes p and s length-n arrays and indexes the n−1 addition steps.",
